compound.name: propylparaben
compound.role: Consumer preservative/exposure; not nominated as a therapeutic.

mouse_oocyte_source.title: Propylparaben exposure impairs G2/M and metaphase-anaphase transition during mouse oocyte maturation
mouse_oocyte_source.available_depth: Complete PubMed/EPMC abstract; main paper not retrieved.
mouse_oocyte_source.reported_exposure: 600 micromolar propylparaben; exact exposure duration and lower-dose conditions not available from the abstract.
reported_findings: Meiotic resumption arrest and failure of first polar-body extrusion
Mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress and DNA damage
MPF Cyclin B1/CDK1 disruption and G2/M arrest
Spindle morphology disorder and chromosome misalignment associated with unstable microtubules
Impaired microtubule-kinetochore attachment with persistent BUB3/BubR1 spindle-assembly-checkpoint activation
mouse_oocyte_source.bubr1_abundance_or_restoration: Not established by the abstract; checkpoint activation is not evidence of increased functional BUBR1.

blood_biomonitoring.sample: 139 paired serum and whole-blood samples from Chinese adults
blood_biomonitoring.notes: Cross-sectional biomonitoring; not ovarian tissue, children with MVA, or lifetime exposure.

human_oral_pharmacokinetics.notes: Controlled labelled-compound doses, not typical consumer-use exposure; abstract gives no MVA or reproductive outcome.

nominal_exposure_comparison.method: 600 micromolar × 180.20 g/mol = 108.12 mg/L = 108,120 ng/mL; ratios compare nominal culture-medium concentration with separate total-serum measurements.
nominal_exposure_comparison.interpretation_limit: Cross-study, cross-matrix magnitude context only; not an internal-dose equivalence, exposure margin, or safety threshold.

competitive_consequence.mva_efficacy: Not established; no actual BUB1B allele or MVA model was tested.
competitive_consequence.rationale: The oocyte study reports high-concentration meiotic injury with checkpoint activation. It does not show rescue or ordinary-use risk in MVA.
